costInfo.costBreakdownTooltip: Costs shown cover only the simulated time window, not a full year. Equipment costs are spread over the equipment lifetime, while running costs (e.g., grid electricity purchases) reflect actual usage during the period. In short simulations, technologies with high running costs appear proportionally larger.
costInfo.equipmentCostNote: Equipment cost is spread over its lifetime, showing only the share for this simulation period.

costInfo.runningCostDesc: Electricity purchased from the grid, maintenance, and other ongoing expenses that depend on usage.

costInfo.lcoeComparisonDesc: Compares the cost of energy from each source in ct/kWh. Solar and wind have low costs because sunlight and wind are free — you only pay for the equipment. The dashed line shows the system-wide average.
costInfo.investmentBreakdownDesc: Shows how much each technology costs, split into equipment (one-time purchase, spread over lifetime) and running costs (grid electricity, maintenance). Renewables typically only have equipment costs.

hero.subtitle: Map industrial emissions, model optimal pipeline & shipping transport networks, evaluate geological storage reservoirs, and fast-track industrial decarbonization across Europe.

challenge.title: Solving European Industrial Decarbonization
challenge.description: Transitioning heavy industry to net-zero requires solving complex spatial, transport, and economic challenges across European borders.
challenge.card1Desc: Heavy industry (cement, steel, chemicals) accounts for over 25% of European emissions, requiring rapid capture deployment.
challenge.card2Desc: Connecting inland industrial clusters to offshore storage requires combining high-pressure pipelines with LCO₂ shipping networks.
challenge.card3Desc: Ensuring long-term containment integrity and matching annual capture volumes to offshore aquifer injection limits.
challenge.card4Desc: Calculating levelized cost of CO₂ avoided (€/t CO₂) across CAPEX, compression power, shipping charters, and carbon taxes.

features.label: Platform Capabilities
features.title: Everything you need for CCUS planning & route optimization
features.description: A comprehensive geospatial toolkit for modeling carbon capture, CO₂ transport logistics, and geological storage reservoirs.
features.f1Desc: Visualize industrial emission sources, pipeline corridors, shipping routes and storage sites in one interactive map.
features.f2Desc: Match industrial CO₂ emitters to suitable geological storage by capacity, distance and cost.
features.f3Desc: Model pipeline and shipping corridors and compute least-cost, carbon-optimal transport routing and sizing.
features.f4Desc: Evaluate deep saline aquifers and depleted oil & gas fields for capacity, pressure limits and injection rates.
features.f5Desc: Levelized cost of CO₂ avoided (€/t) with CAPEX, compression and shipping breakdowns and Sankey carbon flows.
features.f6Desc: Share models, compare scenarios and collaborate with regional consortiums on decarbonization plans.

infrastructure.title: Four stages, one integrated model
infrastructure.description: Capture, transport, storage and utilization — modeled end to end so every project is planned as a complete value chain.
infrastructure.c1Desc: Capture CO₂ at cement, steel, chemical and power plants using post-combustion and other proven technologies.
infrastructure.c2Desc: Move captured CO₂ from inland clusters to storage via high-pressure pipelines and liquefied-CO₂ shipping.
infrastructure.c3Desc: Assess offshore and onshore reservoirs for safe, permanent geological containment of injected CO₂.
infrastructure.c4Desc: Convert captured CO₂ into e-fuels, chemicals, building materials and other valuable products.

howItWorks.label: 4-Step Workflow
howItWorks.title: From site data to operational CCUS network
howItWorks.description: Design, optimize, and deploy carbon capture and storage infrastructure in four steps.
howItWorks.s1Desc: Draw or pick an area on the map. Industrial emitters, storage sites and existing infrastructure load automatically.
howItWorks.s2Desc: Attach capture to emitters, then choose pipeline corridors, shipping terminals and candidate storage reservoirs.
howItWorks.s3Desc: Run the optimization engine to compute least-cost transport routing, network capacity and compression needs.
howItWorks.s4Desc: Explore maps, CO₂ flow diagrams and levelized cost (€/t CO₂), then export reports and share scenarios.

personas.title: Designed for the entire CCUS ecosystem
personas.p1Desc: Cement, steel, chemical, and power plants evaluating point-source capture feasibility and regional trunk connections.
personas.p2Desc: Route high-pressure CO₂ trunk lines, size compressor stations, and optimize ship chartering logistics.
personas.p3Desc: Analyze offshore North Sea, Baltic, and Mediterranean deep saline aquifers for injection rate limits.
personas.p4Desc: Simulate regional net-zero roadmaps, cross-border CO₂ transport regulations, and EU Taxonomy compliance.

trust.euDescription: This CCUS assessment platform is developed as part of an EU-funded Horizon research project accelerating industrial decarbonization across Europe.

registry.layer2Subtitle: Pick the CO₂ sources and sinks

stepper.introDesc: Six guided steps to define your area, validate inputs and launch a analysis run.
stepper.introProgressSaved: Your progress is saved as you go

layer1.purpose: Name this analysis run and choose the date window you want to assess.
layer1.nextStepHint: Next you'll outline the geographic area on the map.
layer1.modelNameHint: A descriptive name so you can find this model later.
layer1.dynamicHint: Dynamic runs keep the selected date range and use the 16:00 to 17:00 window.
layer1.dynamicSelectInside: Select a range inside available dynamic dates: {{start}} to {{end}}
layer1.modelNameQuestion: What do you want to call this model?

layer2.purpose: Choose the CO₂ sources and sinks this model routes between.
layer2.nextStepHint: Next CO2RouteX looks for connections between them.
layer2.nodesQuestion: Which nodes should the model use?
layer2.nodesInfo: Pick them here or straight from the map.
layer2.blockingSelectNodes: Select at least one node to continue.

layer3.purpose: CO2RouteX screens the selected nodes for candidate connections, then routes and costs them.
layer3.nextStepHint: Next you'll see what those routes cost.
layer3.customDataDesc: Bring your own weather inputs for this area. If left empty, the bundled regional data is used.
layer3.lockedByPrecomputed: Included in the precomputed regional map. Disable the precomputed switch above to customise layers.
layer3.precomputedUnavailable: The nightly analysis has not processed this date yet. The model will compute all steps for your area.
layer3.precomputedOffHint: Full computation for your exact area (~1-2 minutes); you can toggle individual layers below.
layer3.routesInfo: One route per source-sink pair, by pipeline, truck or railway.

layer4.purpose: Pipeline CAPEX scales with route resistance; truck and railway use distance tariffs.
layer4.nextStepHint: Next we'll do a final review before saving.
layer4.dynamicRequiresBefore: Dynamic mode requires start before end.
layer4.dynamicUnavailableDates: The selected dynamic date range contains unavailable dates.
layer4.noPolygon: No polygon drawn on the map.
layer4.allSignalsActive: All risk signals active (weather + terrain + history).
layer4.someSignalsActive: Running with {{count}} of 3 optional signals — output will differ from the full model.
layer4.allPassed: All checks passed. Ready to save & calculate.
layer4.costsInfo: Calculated from the routes found in the previous step.
layer4.noNodes: No nodes selected — go back to Step 2.

layer5.purpose: Review the model setup before saving. The calculation will use the selected dates, area and data source choices.
layer5.dailyRunInfo: Every simulated day is assessed with the weather from this window — the hottest, driest part of the afternoon.

coverage.title: Data coverage
coverage.blankDesc: Blank areas have no valid source raster data for calculation.

blocking.dynamicOrder: The start date must be before or equal to the end date.
